description: Error status for the search index aggregation job; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; its child indexing job failed.

translation: {{.Backend}} failed to backfill channel type on posts
description: Error status for a maintenance job; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; it failed to fill in the channel type field on indexed posts.

translation: Could not open the CA file for {{.Backend}}
description: Admin-facing error when connecting to the search backend; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; 'CA file' is the certificate authority file configured in the System Console.

translation: Decoding of the client certificate for {{.Backend}} failed
description: Admin-facing error when the configured TLS client certificate for the search backend cannot be decoded; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Could not open the client certificate file for {{.Backend}}
description: Admin-facing error when the configured TLS client certificate file for the search backend cannot be opened; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Could not open the client key file for {{.Backend}}
description: Admin-facing error when the configured TLS client key file for the search backend cannot be opened; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Setting up {{.Backend}} client failed.
description: Admin-facing error when the connection client for the search backend cannot be created; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Failed to create Elasticsearch bulk processor
description: Admin-facing error when starting Elasticsearch integration; 'bulk processor' is a technical component that batches index writes.

translation: Failed to create Elasticsearch sync bulk processor
description: Admin-facing error when starting Elasticsearch integration; the 'sync bulk processor' is a technical component for synchronous batched writes.

translation: Failed to create {{.Backend}} template for channels
description: Admin-facing error while setting up search; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; 'template' is an index template for the channels index.

translation: Failed to create {{.Backend}} template for files
description: Admin-facing error while setting up search; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; 'template' is an index template for the files index.

translation: Failed to create {{.Backend}} template for posts. Verify that the required analysis-icu plugin is installed on every {{.Backend}} node, then restart {{.Backend}}
description: Admin-facing error while setting up search; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; 'template' is an index template for the posts index.

translation: Failed to create {{.Backend}} template for users
description: Admin-facing error while setting up search; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; 'template' is an index template for the users index.

translation: Failed to delete {{.Backend}} index
description: Error from the data retention job when deleting an old search index fails; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Failed to get {{.Backend}} indexes
description: Error from the data retention job when listing search indices fails; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Failed to delete the channel
description: Error when removing a deleted channel from the search index fails; 'channel' is a Mattermost channel document in the index.

translation: Failed to delete channel posts
description: Error when removing a deleted channel's posts (messages) from the search index fails.

translation: Failed to delete file
description: Error when removing a deleted file from the search index fails.

translation: Failed to delete files batch
description: Error when bulk-deleting a batch of file documents from the OpenSearch index fails.

translation: Failed to delete the post
description: Error when removing a deleted post (message) from the search index fails.

translation: Failed to delete post files
description: Error when removing a deleted post's file attachments from the search index fails.

translation: Failed to delete the user
description: Error when removing a deleted user from the search index fails.

translation: Failed to delete user files
description: Error when removing a deleted user's files from the search index fails.

translation: Failed to delete user posts
description: Error when removing a deleted user's posts (messages) from the search index fails.

translation: {{.Backend}} search is not enabled on this server
description: Error returned when a search-backend operation is attempted while the feature is turned off; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Failed to get all channel members
description: Error status for the search indexing job when channel members cannot be read from the database while indexing a channel.

translation: Failed to get all team members
description: Error status for the search indexing job when team members cannot be read from the database while indexing a channel.

translation: {{.Backend}} is not started.
description: Health check error shown to admins (e.g. in the System Console connection test); {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: {{.Backend}} health check failed: could not complete check.
description: Health check error shown to admins when the search backend cannot be reached; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Failed to index the channel
description: Error when writing a channel document to the search index fails; 'index' is a verb.

translation: Unable to get the channels batch for indexing.
description: Error status for the search indexing job when a batch of channels cannot be read from the database.

translation: Failed to index the file
description: Error when writing a file document to the search index fails; 'index' is a verb.

translation: Failed to index the post
description: Error when writing a post (message) document to the search index fails; 'index' is a verb.

translation: Failed to index the user
description: Error when writing a user document to the search index fails; 'index' is a verb.

translation: Indexing job completed but {{.NumFailed}} document(s) were rejected by the search backend and not indexed
description: Warning status on a completed search indexing job; {{.NumFailed}} is the number of documents the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch backend rejected.

translation: Indexing worker failed to initialize the bulk processor.
description: Error status when the search indexing job cannot initialize its bulk-write component; 'bulk processor' is a technical component name.

translation: The oldest entity (user, channel or post) could not be retrieved from the database.
description: Error status when the search indexing job cannot determine the oldest record to index; the parenthetical lists the entity kinds.

translation: {{.Backend}} indexing worker failed to parse the end time
description: Error status for the search indexing job; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; the end time is a job parameter bounding what is indexed.

translation: {{.Backend}} indexing worker failed to parse the start time
description: Error status for the search indexing job; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; the start time is a job parameter bounding what is indexed.

translation: Trying to index a new batch when all the entities are completed
description: Internal error status for the search indexing job when it is asked to index another batch although every entity type has finished.

translation: {{.Backend}} is not started.
description: Error returned when a search operation is attempted before the backend integration has started; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Unable to get the files batch for indexing.
description: Error status for the search indexing job when a batch of file records cannot be read from the database.

translation: Unable to get the posts batch for indexing.
description: Error status for the search indexing job when a batch of posts cannot be read from the database; 'posts' are messages.

translation: Failed to delete a search index
description: Admin-facing error when the purge-indexes action fails to delete a search index (e.g. via System Console or mmctl).

translation: Failed to delete an unknown index specified
description: Admin-facing error when the purge-indexes action is given an index name that does not exist.

translation: Failed to refresh search indexes
description: Error when refreshing the search indices (making recent writes searchable) fails; 'refresh' is an Elasticsearch operation.

translation: {{.Backend}} searching is disabled on this server
description: Error returned when channel search is attempted while search is disabled; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Search failed to complete
description: Error returned to the user when a channel search query against the search backend fails.

translation: Failed to decode search results
description: Error when the channel search results returned by the search backend cannot be decoded.

translation: {{.Backend}} files searching is disabled on this server
description: Error returned when file search is attempted while it is disabled; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Search failed to complete
description: Error returned to the user when a file search query against the search backend fails.

translation: Failed to decode search results
description: Error when the file search results returned by the search backend cannot be decoded.

translation: {{.Backend}} searching is disabled on this server
description: Error returned when message search is attempted while search is disabled; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Search failed to complete
description: Error returned to the user when a message search query against the search backend fails.

translation: Failed to decode search results
description: Error when the message search results returned by the search backend cannot be decoded.

translation: Search failed to complete
description: Error returned when a user search query against the search backend fails.

translation: Failed to decode search results
description: Error when the user search results returned by the search backend cannot be decoded.

translation: Failed to get {{.Backend}} server version.
description: Admin-facing error when the search backend's version cannot be fetched at startup; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Failed to parse {{.Backend}} server version.
description: Admin-facing error when the search backend's reported version string cannot be parsed; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: {{.Backend}} is disabled.
description: Error from the System Console connection test when the search feature is disabled in settings; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'.

translation: Your Mattermost license doesn't support indexed search.
description: Admin console error when testing the Elasticsearch/search connection on a license tier that does not include indexed search.

translation: The Search Server URL or Username has changed. Please re-enter the password to test connection.
description: Admin console error on the Elasticsearch settings page: after changing the server URL or username, the admin must re-type the password before using the 'Test Connection' button. 'Search Server URL' and 'Username' are setting labels.

translation: {{.Backend}} failed to update channel type on posts
description: Error status for a maintenance job; {{.Backend}} is 'Elasticsearch' or 'OpenSearch'; it failed to update the channel type field on indexed posts.

translation: Your license does not support ID Loaded Push Notifications.
description: Error when ID-only ('ID Loaded') push notifications are configured without a supporting license; 'ID Loaded Push Notifications' is a feature name; admin audience.

translation: Your account isn't fully set up yet. Please sign in to Mattermost via the web or desktop app first.
description: Error shown on the mobile app sign-in flow via Microsoft Intune when no matching Mattermost account exists yet; end-user audience.

translation: Authentication failed. Please try again or contact your system administrator.
description: Error shown to end users when Microsoft Intune sign-in fails while reading identity data from the token.

translation: Microsoft Intune authentication is not configured.
description: Error shown when a user attempts Microsoft Intune sign-in but the server has not configured it; 'Intune' is a Microsoft product name.

translation: Authentication failed. Invalid configuration.
description: Error shown to end users during Microsoft Intune sign-in when the server's tenant configuration is wrong; intentionally vague for security.

translation: Authentication failed. Please try again.
description: Error shown to end users when the Microsoft Intune sign-in token fails validation.

translation: Authentication service initialization failed. Please contact your system administrator.
description: Error shown to end users when the server cannot initialize key retrieval (JWKS) for validating Microsoft Intune sign-in tokens.

translation: Authentication failed. Required user information is missing.
description: Error shown to end users when the Microsoft Intune sign-in token lacks required identity fields (claims).

translation: Authentication session has expired. Please try signing in again.
description: Error shown to end users when their Microsoft Intune sign-in token has expired; invites them to sign in again.

translation: Reached AD/LDAP synchronization job timeout.
description: Error when a manually triggered AD/LDAP synchronization job does not finish within the allowed time; admin audience.

translation: ldap interface was nil.
description: Internal server error logged/returned when the enterprise LDAP module is not loaded; mostly seen by admins/developers.

translation: LDAP connection test failed. Server: {{.Server}}:{{.Port}}, ConnectionSecurity: {{.ConnectionType}}, PrivateKeyFilename: {{.PrivateKeyFilename}}, PublicCertificateFilename: {{.PublicCertFilename}}, BindUsername: {{.BindUsername}}. Error: {{.Error}}
description: Result message of the AD/LDAP connection test in the System Console; placeholders hold the configured server host, port, security type, certificate file names, bind username, and the underlying error.

translation: Unable to create LDAP user.
description: Error when the server fails to create a Mattermost account for an AD/LDAP user (e.g. during first login or sync).

translation: AD/LDAP disabled or license does not support AD/LDAP.
description: API error shown to admins when an AD/LDAP operation is attempted but AD/LDAP is disabled or unlicensed.

translation: Unable to bind to AD/LDAP server. Check BindUsername and BindPassword.
description: AD/LDAP sign-in error for admins; 'bind', 'BindUsername', and 'BindPassword' are LDAP terms/setting names and should stay recognizable.

translation: Error loading LDAP TLS Certificate file.
description: Error when the TLS certificate file configured for AD/LDAP connections cannot be loaded; admin audience.

translation: Invalid AD/LDAP Id
description: Error during AD/LDAP sign-in when the user's directory ID attribute value is invalid; 'Id' is the LDAP ID attribute.

translation: Invalid Password.
description: Error shown on the login page when an AD/LDAP user enters a wrong password.

translation: Error loading LDAP TLS Key file.
description: Error when the TLS private key file configured for AD/LDAP connections cannot be loaded; admin audience.

translation: AD/LDAP functionality disabled by current license. Please contact your system administrator about upgrading your enterprise license.

translation: No audit log target is active and this workspace has {{.users}} registered users. Administrative actions, logins and configuration changes leave no separate audit trail. This is a compliance and forensic gap, not a stability risk.

translation: If your organization has audit requirements (financial services, healthcare, defense, regulated public sector), enable audit logging in System Console > Compliance > Audit Logging, or add a target for the audit levels to ExperimentalAuditSettings.AdvancedLoggingJSON, and configure rotation. Otherwise this can be ignored.

translation: Audit logging disabled
description: Health dashboard finding title when no audit log target is active.

translation: ServiceSettings.ListenAddress binds port {{.port}}, which is below 1024. On Linux, a Mattermost server that does not run as root can bind this port only through the CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE file capability on its binary. A package upgrade replaces the binary and clears that capability, so the server can fail to start after the next upgrade with "bind: permission denied". The configuration cannot show how the capability is granted, so this warning stays even after you grant it through the systemd unit.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the server listens on a privileged port (below 1024); {{.port}} is the port number. 'ServiceSettings.ListenAddress' is a config setting path, 'CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE' is a Linux capability name and 'bind: permission denied' is a literal error message; do not translate them.

translation: Add AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE to the Mattermost systemd unit so the capability survives upgrades, or re-run setcap CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE=+eip /opt/mattermost/bin/mattermost after every upgrade. Alternatively, put a reverse proxy in front of Mattermost and bind Mattermost to a high port such as 8065.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a server that listens on a privileged port; 'AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE' is a systemd setting and the setcap command is a literal shell command; do not translate them.

translation: Server binds a privileged port directly
description: Health dashboard finding title when the server listens on a port below 1024 itself instead of behind a reverse proxy.

translation: The leader advertises {{.address}}. Other nodes cannot reach it at that address, so gossip forms a one-node cluster and split brains are hidden.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the cluster advertise address is a loopback, unspecified or localhost address; {{.address}} is the configured address, and 'gossip' is the protocol cluster nodes use to talk to each other.

translation: Set ClusterSettings.AdvertiseAddress to the node's reachable IP address or DNS name, or leave it empty to use the network interface address. This check reads the leader's configuration, so review the setting on every node.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for an unreachable cluster advertise address; 'ClusterSettings.AdvertiseAddress' is the config setting path and should not be translated, and 'leader' is the cluster node that runs the health check.

translation: ClusterSettings.AdvertiseAddress is not reachable from other nodes
description: Health dashboard finding title when the cluster advertise address is a loopback, unspecified or localhost address; 'ClusterSettings.AdvertiseAddress' is the config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: The configuration is stored in a file on each node and can be changed in the System Console. A change is saved on one node and pushed to the others on a best-effort basis; a node that misses the push keeps its own file, so the nodes' configurations can drift apart.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a high availability cluster uses file-based configuration that the System Console can change; 'System Console' is the Mattermost admin UI.

translation: Set ClusterSettings.ReadOnlyConfig to true and manage the configuration through the config file or environment variables on every node, or move the configuration into the database.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a writable file-based configuration in a high availability cluster; 'ClusterSettings.ReadOnlyConfig' is the config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: ClusterSettings.ReadOnlyConfig is off in a file-based HA cluster
description: Health dashboard finding title when a high availability cluster with file-based configuration allows configuration changes from the System Console; 'ClusterSettings.ReadOnlyConfig' is the config setting path and should not be translated, and 'HA' means high availability.

translation: ClusterSettings.EnableGossipEncryption is false, so traffic between cluster nodes is not encrypted.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when cluster gossip encryption is turned off; 'ClusterSettings.EnableGossipEncryption' is the config setting path and should not be translated, and 'gossip' is the protocol cluster nodes use to talk to each other.

translation: Enable gossip encryption, then restart all nodes together in a maintenance window. Nodes with and without encryption cannot talk to each other, so a rolling restart splits the cluster until the last node restarts.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for unencrypted cluster gossip; 'gossip' is the protocol cluster nodes use to talk to each other.

translation: HA cluster gossip is not encrypted
description: Health dashboard finding title when cluster gossip encryption is turned off; 'HA' means high availability, and 'gossip' is the protocol cluster nodes use to talk to each other.

translation: With {{.users}} registered users on HA, the default in-memory LRU cache means each node maintains its own copy and uses gossip for invalidation. Mattermost recommends Redis at 100,000 users and above to reduce cache-invalidation traffic at this scale.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a large high availability cluster uses the in-memory cache; {{.users}} is the registered user count, 'LRU' and 'Redis' are cache backend names and should not be translated, and 'gossip' is the protocol cluster nodes use to talk to each other.

translation: Evaluate setting CacheSettings.CacheType to redis with CacheSettings.RedisAddress configured. Redis requires a license with the Cluster feature.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a large cluster on the in-memory cache; 'CacheSettings.CacheType', 'CacheSettings.RedisAddress' and 'redis' are config names and values and should not be translated.

translation: At scale, consider the Redis cache backend
description: Health dashboard finding title suggesting the Redis cache for a large high availability cluster; 'Redis' is a product name and should not be translated.

translation: The intended HA topology is not actually running. A single node gives no failover and hides split-brain risk.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when high availability is enabled but the cluster has only one node; 'HA' means high availability, and 'split-brain' is when cluster nodes lose contact and act independently.

translation: Check gossip connectivity (ClusterSettings.GossipPort), firewall rules, and that all app nodes share the same ClusterName. An empty ClusterName also keeps the node on its own: the server then logs that high availability has been disabled.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a cluster with only one node; 'ClusterSettings.GossipPort' and 'ClusterName' are config setting names and should not be translated, and 'gossip' is the protocol cluster nodes use to talk to each other.

translation: High availability is enabled but only one node is in the cluster
description: Health dashboard finding title when ClusterSettings.Enable is on but the cluster reports a single node.

translation: Nodes in the cluster report these versions: {{.versions}}.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when cluster nodes run different Mattermost versions; {{.versions}} is a comma-separated list of the versions.

translation: The nodes are split between versions, with no version more common than the others, so it is not clear which nodes are out of date.
description: Health dashboard reason shown for one cluster node when two or more versions are tied for the most common version, so the node's status is unknown.

translation: This node runs {{.version}}, while most nodes run {{.majority}}.
description: Health dashboard finding detail for one cluster node that runs a different Mattermost version; {{.version}} is the node's version and {{.majority}} is the version most nodes run.

translation: Unless an upgrade is in progress, upgrade every node to the same version and make sure the nodes can communicate via gossip.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for cluster nodes on different versions; 'gossip' is the protocol cluster nodes use to talk to each other.

translation: Multiple Mattermost versions detected in the cluster
description: Health dashboard finding title when cluster nodes run different Mattermost versions.

translation: ComplianceSettings.Directory is empty, so compliance reports are written to a compliance folder under the server's working directory. They are lost when the server is upgraded or its container is rebuilt.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when compliance monitoring is on but its report directory is empty; 'ComplianceSettings.Directory' is a config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: Set Compliance Report Directory in System Console > Compliance > Compliance Monitoring (ComplianceSettings.Directory) to a persistent, writable path.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for an empty compliance report directory; 'System Console > Compliance > Compliance Monitoring' is a navigation path and 'ComplianceSettings.Directory' is a config setting path that should not be translated.

translation: Compliance monitoring enabled but Directory is empty
description: Health dashboard finding title when compliance monitoring is turned on but the compliance report directory is empty.

translation: Each node keeps a pool of up to MaxOpenConns connections to the primary. With {{.nodes}} nodes and MaxOpenConns={{.max_open}}, a database failover can produce up to {{.burst}} simultaneous connection attempts to the newly promoted primary, and the DataSource host does not look like a connection pooler. If that exceeds the database's max_connections, it rejects connections ('sorry, too many clients already') and recovery takes longer.
description: Health dashboard finding detail for the risk of a reconnection burst after a database failover in a cluster; {{.nodes}}, {{.max_open}}, {{.data_sources}} and {{.burst}} are numbers. 'MaxOpenConns', 'DataSource' and 'max_connections' are setting names and 'sorry, too many clients already' is a literal PostgreSQL error; do not translate them.

translation: Size every layer against this burst. The most durable fix is to lower SqlSettings.MaxOpenConns per node and/or put PgBouncer (transaction mode) in front of the database to absorb reconnection bursts, rather than only raising max_connections: each connection costs database memory, so a high ceiling risks running out of memory. If max_connections is raised, keep headroom above the burst for replication, monitoring, and admin sessions. Staggering node startup during a failover also keeps the burst below the ceiling.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for the risk of a reconnection burst after a database failover. 'SqlSettings.MaxOpenConns' and 'max_connections' are setting names and 'PgBouncer' is a product name; do not translate them.

translation: Database failover can cause a connection storm
description: Health dashboard finding title when a database failover could make every cluster node reconnect at once and exceed the database's connection limit.

translation: SqlSettings.MaxIdleConns ({{.max_idle}}) is set higher than MaxOpenConns ({{.max_open}}). Go's database/sql layer silently caps the idle pool at MaxOpenConns, so the extra idle capacity has no effect. Nothing is broken, but the value is misleading and usually indicates the pool was tuned without knowing that idle can never exceed open.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the idle connection limit is above the open connection limit; {{.max_idle}} and {{.max_open}} are numbers. 'SqlSettings.MaxIdleConns', 'MaxOpenConns' and 'database/sql' are technical names and should not be translated.

translation: Set MaxIdleConns to a value at or below MaxOpenConns (a common guideline is 25-50% of MaxOpenConns).
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the idle connection limit is above the open connection limit. 'MaxIdleConns' and 'MaxOpenConns' are setting names and should not be translated.

translation: MaxIdleConns exceeds MaxOpenConns
description: Health dashboard finding title when the idle database connection limit is set above the open connection limit. 'MaxIdleConns' and 'MaxOpenConns' are setting names and should not be translated.

translation: With {{.users}} users and MaxOpenConns={{.max_open}}, request queueing on the app side is possible under burst load. The current default is 100 (MaxIdleConns 50, a 2:1 ratio).
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the database connection limit is low for the number of users; {{.users}} and {{.max_open}} are numbers. 'MaxOpenConns' and 'MaxIdleConns' are setting names and should not be translated.

translation: If app-side request queueing is observed, raise SqlSettings.MaxOpenConns based on monitored need (the 100/50 defaults are the baseline). The real database ceiling is MaxOpenConns x nodes x data sources, so confirm the database's max_connections covers that total before raising it.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the database connection limit is low for the number of users. 'SqlSettings.MaxOpenConns', 'MaxOpenConns' and 'max_connections' are setting names and should not be translated.

translation: MaxOpenConns may be low for this user base
description: Health dashboard finding title when the database connection limit may be too low for the number of users. 'MaxOpenConns' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: SqlSettings.DataSourceReplicas is empty. With {{.users}} users, all reads hit the primary. Read replicas are recommended for larger deployments.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when no database read replica is configured on a large deployment; {{.users}} is the number of registered users. 'SqlSettings.DataSourceReplicas' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: Consider provisioning a read replica and adding it to SqlSettings.DataSourceReplicas.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when no database read replica is configured. 'SqlSettings.DataSourceReplicas' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: No read replicas configured
description: Health dashboard finding title when no database read replica is configured.

translation: With {{.posts}} posts and database search, the primary and replicas absorb full-text scans. This causes CPU pressure and search timeouts at this scale.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when search runs on the database without a search replica on a large deployment; {{.posts}} is the number of posts.

translation: With {{.posts}} posts and database search, the primary and replicas absorb full-text scans. This causes CPU pressure and search timeouts at this scale. Your license includes Elasticsearch, which takes search off the database entirely.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when search runs on the database without a search replica on a large deployment whose license includes Elasticsearch; {{.posts}} is the number of posts. 'Elasticsearch' is a product name and should not be translated.

translation: Configure SqlSettings.DataSourceSearchReplicas.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when search runs on the database without a search replica. 'SqlSettings.DataSourceSearchReplicas' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: No search replica and Elasticsearch search disabled
description: Health dashboard finding title when there is no database search replica and Elasticsearch is not used for search. 'Elasticsearch' is a product name and should not be translated.

translation: {{.in_use}} of {{.max_open}} primary database connections are in use ({{.percent}}%), at or above 90% of MaxOpenConns. New queries will queue and HTTP latency rises.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the primary database connection pool is nearly full; {{.in_use}}, {{.max_open}} and {{.percent}} are numbers. 'MaxOpenConns' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: Raise SqlSettings.MaxOpenConns and the database's max_connections. Also investigate long-running queries.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the primary database connection pool is nearly full. 'SqlSettings.MaxOpenConns' and 'max_connections' are setting names and should not be translated.

translation: Database primary pool near saturation
description: Health dashboard finding title when most connections in the primary database connection pool are in use.

translation: PostgreSQL {{.version}} is below the minimum supported version. Mattermost requires PostgreSQL {{.minimum}} or later.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the database runs an unsupported PostgreSQL version; {{.version}} is the reported server version and {{.minimum}} is the minimum major version. 'PostgreSQL' is a product name and should not be translated.

translation: Plan an upgrade. Newer versions also ship better parallel query and JSONB performance.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the database runs an unsupported PostgreSQL version. 'JSONB' is a PostgreSQL data type and should not be translated.

translation: PostgreSQL version is below the minimum supported
description: Health dashboard finding title when the database runs a PostgreSQL version older than Mattermost supports. 'PostgreSQL' is a product name and should not be translated.

translation: QueryTimeout is set to {{.timeout}} seconds. Long timeouts let runaway queries hold locks for the full duration, blocking autovacuum, schema migrations, and writers behind the same row. This compounds risk on busy databases without read replicas.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the database query timeout is high; {{.timeout}} is a number of seconds. 'QueryTimeout' is a setting name and 'autovacuum' is a PostgreSQL process; do not translate them.

translation: Reduce SqlSettings.QueryTimeout to 30. Investigate any specific slow queries separately rather than raising the global ceiling.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the database query timeout is high. 'SqlSettings.QueryTimeout' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: SqlSettings.QueryTimeout is high (default is 30s)
description: Health dashboard finding title when the database query timeout is well above its 30 second default. 'SqlSettings.QueryTimeout' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: DataSourceReplicas is set but no replica is reachable, so reads are falling back to the primary.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when read replicas are configured but none is reachable. 'DataSourceReplicas' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: Verify the replica DSN, network reachability, and authentication. Check the server logs for replica connection warnings.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when read replicas are configured but none is reachable; 'DSN' means the database connection string.

translation: Read replicas configured but none reachable
description: Health dashboard finding title when read replicas are configured but none is reachable.

translation: Every SQL statement is logged. This is intended for debugging only: leaving it on fills the disk and writes query payloads to the log files.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when SQL statement tracing is enabled.

translation: Set SqlSettings.Trace to false unless actively debugging.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when SQL statement tracing is enabled. 'SqlSettings.Trace' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: SqlSettings.Trace is enabled
description: Health dashboard finding title when SQL statement tracing is enabled. 'SqlSettings.Trace' is a setting name and should not be translated.

translation: The server runs on {{.os}}. Mattermost supports Linux for production; other operating systems are suitable for development only.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the server does not run on Linux; {{.os}} is the operating system name reported by Go, such as windows or darwin.

translation: Move the server to a supported Linux distribution.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a server running on an operating system other than Linux.

translation: Server is not running on Linux
description: Health dashboard finding title when the Mattermost server runs on an operating system other than Linux.

translation: Each new post is indexed synchronously with its own request. On busy servers this overloads the search cluster and delays indexing.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when LiveIndexingBatchSize is 1.

translation: Raise LiveIndexingBatchSize to between 10 and 20, and tune within that range based on the observed post rate.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when LiveIndexingBatchSize is 1; 'LiveIndexingBatchSize' is a config setting name and should not be translated.

translation: Elasticsearch LiveIndexingBatchSize is 1
description: Health dashboard finding title when live indexing is configured to index each post on its own; 'LiveIndexingBatchSize' is a config setting name and should not be translated.

translation: LiveIndexingBatchSize is {{.size}}. Large _bulk requests can exceed the search cluster's http.max_content_length and fail with 413 errors, causing retries and indexing lag.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when LiveIndexingBatchSize is above 100; {{.size}} is the configured value. '_bulk', 'http.max_content_length' and '413' are literal technical terms and should not be translated.

translation: Lower LiveIndexingBatchSize to between 10 and 20, or raise http.max_content_length on the search cluster if very large batches are intentional.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when LiveIndexingBatchSize is above 100; 'LiveIndexingBatchSize' and 'http.max_content_length' are setting names and should not be translated.

translation: Elasticsearch LiveIndexingBatchSize is above 100
description: Health dashboard finding title when live indexing batches are large; 'LiveIndexingBatchSize' is a config setting name and should not be translated.

translation: ConnectionURL points to {{.host}}, which each app node resolves to itself. Nodes without a local search engine cannot index or search.
description: Health dashboard finding detail for a loopback search engine URL in a cluster; {{.host}} is the configured host name or IP address. 'ConnectionURL' is a config setting name and should not be translated.

translation: Set ConnectionURL to a hostname or service DNS name that every app node can reach.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a loopback search engine URL in a cluster; 'ConnectionURL' is a config setting name and 'app node' is a Mattermost application server.

translation: Elasticsearch ConnectionURL points to localhost
description: Health dashboard finding title when the search engine connection URL points to the local machine on a clustered server; 'ConnectionURL' is a config setting name and should not be translated.

translation: The search cluster does not report the analysis-icu plugin. The post index template uses the ICU tokenizer and normalizer, so post indexing may fail without it.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the analysis-icu plugin is missing; 'analysis-icu' is a plugin name and 'ICU' a technical term, neither should be translated.

translation: The plugin list was not collected because the server could not read the search cluster version.
description: Health dashboard reason shown when the search engine plugin list is missing, so the check's status is unknown.

translation: Install the analysis-icu plugin on every search node (elasticsearch-plugin install analysis-icu, or opensearch-plugin install analysis-icu), then restart the nodes. Post indexing requires it, not only multilingual search.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the analysis-icu plugin is missing; the commands in parentheses are literal and should not be translated.

translation: Search engine is missing the analysis-icu plugin
description: Health dashboard finding title when the Elasticsearch or OpenSearch cluster does not report the analysis-icu plugin; 'analysis-icu' is a plugin name and should not be translated.

translation: The connection test to the search engine failed: {{.error}}
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the search engine connection test failed; {{.error}} is the error the server reported, with URL credentials masked.

translation: The connection test to the search engine failed and database search is disabled, so search returns no results: {{.error}}
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the search engine connection test failed and SqlSettings.DisableDatabaseSearch is on; {{.error}} is the error the server reported, with URL credentials masked.

translation: The connection test to the search engine failed on {{.nodes}}, while the other nodes reach it, so search and indexing on those nodes may fail. Check the network, firewall, proxy and DNS settings on those nodes. Error: {{.error}}
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the Elasticsearch or OpenSearch connection test fails on some cluster nodes but not others; {{.nodes}} is a comma-separated list of node hostnames and {{.error}} is the error the failing nodes reported.

translation: Verify ElasticsearchSettings.ConnectionURL reachability, TLS, and credentials. Check the search cluster health (GET /_cluster/health).
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a failed search engine connection test; 'ElasticsearchSettings.ConnectionURL' is a config setting name and 'GET /_cluster/health' is a literal API call, neither should be translated.

translation: Server reports an Elasticsearch cluster error
description: Health dashboard finding title when the server's connection test to the Elasticsearch or OpenSearch cluster failed.

translation: SkipTLSVerification is true on an https connection, so the server does not validate the search engine's certificate. This is acceptable on a trusted internal network, but removes protection against a man-in-the-middle elsewhere.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when TLS verification is skipped for the search engine; 'SkipTLSVerification' is a config setting name and should not be translated.

translation: If the search endpoint is on an untrusted path, install its CA so the certificate validates and set SkipTLSVerification to false. On a trusted internal network, confirm the setting is intentional.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when TLS verification is skipped for the search engine; 'SkipTLSVerification' is a config setting name and 'CA' means certificate authority.

translation: Elasticsearch connection skips TLS certificate verification
description: Health dashboard finding title when the server does not verify the search engine's TLS certificate.

translation: {{.backend}} {{.version}} is newer than the supported major versions ({{.min}} to {{.max}}). Upgrade Mattermost to a release that supports it, or move the search cluster back to a supported version.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the search engine major version is above the supported range; {{.backend}} is elasticsearch or opensearch, {{.version}} the reported version, {{.min}} and {{.max}} the supported major versions.

translation: {{.backend}} {{.version}} is older than the supported major versions ({{.min}} to {{.max}}). Upgrade the search cluster to a supported version.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the search engine major version is below the supported range; {{.backend}} is elasticsearch or opensearch, {{.version}} the reported version, {{.min}} and {{.max}} the supported major versions.

translation: The search cluster version was not collected because the server has not connected to the search cluster.
description: Health dashboard reason shown when the server diagnostics carry no search cluster version, for example because the server could not connect to the search cluster, so the check's status is unknown.

translation: The search engine backend or version could not be recognized.
description: Health dashboard reason shown when the search engine backend or version reported in the server diagnostics is unrecognized, so the check's status is unknown.

translation: Run a major version of the search cluster that this Mattermost version supports.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for an Elasticsearch or OpenSearch version that is older or newer than the supported range.

translation: Search engine version is unsupported
description: Health dashboard finding title when the Elasticsearch or OpenSearch cluster runs a major version the server does not support.

translation: GlobalRelaySettings.SMTPServerTimeout is {{.value}} seconds. It limits how long the export waits to connect to the Global Relay SMTP server, and under 30 seconds a slow connection fails the delivery.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the Global Relay SMTP connection timeout is under 30 seconds; {{.value}} is the configured timeout in seconds. 'GlobalRelaySettings.SMTPServerTimeout' is a config setting path and 'Global Relay' is a product name; neither should be translated.

translation: Raise MessageExportSettings.GlobalRelaySettings.SMTPServerTimeout to at least 30 seconds. The default is 1800.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a low Global Relay SMTP timeout; 'MessageExportSettings.GlobalRelaySettings.SMTPServerTimeout' is a config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: Global Relay SMTPServerTimeout is under 30 seconds
description: Health dashboard finding title when the Global Relay message export SMTP timeout is under 30 seconds; 'Global Relay' is a product name and 'SMTPServerTimeout' is a config setting name, neither should be translated.

translation: The volume containing FileSettings.Directory has {{.available_gib}} GiB ({{.percent}}%) available of {{.total_gib}} GiB. File uploads and other file operations can fail when the volume fills.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the local file storage volume has less than 5% and less than 5 GiB available; {{.available_gib}} and {{.total_gib}} are disk sizes in GiB, and {{.percent}} is the available percentage. 'FileSettings.Directory' is a config setting path and 'GiB' is a unit; neither should be translated.

translation: Immediately expand the volume or remove unrelated data from its filesystem; do not manually delete files managed by Mattermost from FileSettings.Directory. Keep at least 10% or 10 GiB available, and never less than 1 GiB.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a critically low local file storage volume. It warns against deleting Mattermost-managed files and gives the free-space target. 'Mattermost' is a product name, 'FileSettings.Directory' is a config setting path and 'GiB' is a unit; none should be translated.

translation: File storage disk is nearly full
description: Health dashboard finding title when a server node's local file storage volume has critically little space available.

translation: The volume containing FileSettings.Directory has {{.available_gib}} GiB ({{.percent}}%) available of {{.total_gib}} GiB.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the local file storage volume has less than 1 GiB available, or less than 10% and less than 10 GiB available, unless the critical disk-space rule applies; {{.available_gib}} and {{.total_gib}} are disk sizes in GiB, and {{.percent}} is the available percentage. 'FileSettings.Directory' is a config setting path and 'GiB' is a unit; neither should be translated.

translation: Expand the volume or remove unrelated data from its filesystem; do not manually delete files managed by Mattermost from FileSettings.Directory. Keep at least 10% or 10 GiB available, and never less than 1 GiB.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a local file storage volume with low available space. It warns against deleting Mattermost-managed files and gives the free-space target. 'Mattermost' is a product name, 'FileSettings.Directory' is a config setting path and 'GiB' is a unit; none should be translated.

translation: File storage disk space is low
description: Health dashboard finding title when a server node's local file storage volume has low available space.

translation: FileSettings.DriverName is local with ClusterSettings.Enable on, and FileSettings.Directory is {{.directory}}. In a cluster this directory must be a shared mount (NFS, EFS, GlusterFS, CephFS) mounted identically on every node, or files uploaded to one node are not visible on the others. The configuration cannot show whether the directory is shared, and a node can pass the file storage connection test while writing to its own local disk.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a high availability cluster stores files in a local directory that may or may not be a shared mount; {{.directory}} is the configured directory. 'FileSettings.DriverName', 'ClusterSettings.Enable' and 'FileSettings.Directory' are config setting paths, 'local' is a setting value, and NFS, EFS, GlusterFS and CephFS are shared file system names; do not translate them.

translation: On every app node, run findmnt with the FileSettings.Directory path. A relative path resolves against the Mattermost working directory, usually /opt/mattermost. Every node must show the same remote source, and the Mattermost user must be able to read and write there. If the directory is not a shared mount, move it to one or switch FileSettings.DriverName to amazons3.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step asking the admin to confirm that the file storage directory is a shared mount on every node; 'findmnt' is a Linux command, '/opt/mattermost' is a path and 'amazons3' is a setting value; do not translate them.

translation: Local file storage in a high availability cluster: confirm the shared mount
description: Health dashboard finding title asking the admin to confirm that a cluster's local file storage directory is shared by every node.

translation: FileSettings.AmazonS3Bucket is empty, so file uploads fail.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when Amazon S3 file storage is selected without a bucket name; 'FileSettings.AmazonS3Bucket' is a config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: Set FileSettings.AmazonS3Bucket, along with the region and endpoint.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for Amazon S3 file storage without a bucket name; 'FileSettings.AmazonS3Bucket' is a config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: Amazon S3 file storage selected but the bucket is blank
description: Health dashboard finding title when file storage uses Amazon S3 but no bucket name is set.

translation: FileSettings.AmazonS3SSL is false, so files travel between the server and the S3 endpoint unencrypted.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when Amazon S3 file storage has SSL turned off; 'FileSettings.AmazonS3SSL' is a config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: Set FileSettings.AmazonS3SSL to true, unless the endpoint only supports plain HTTP.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for Amazon S3 file storage with SSL turned off; 'FileSettings.AmazonS3SSL' is a config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: Amazon S3 SSL disabled
description: Health dashboard finding title when file storage connects to Amazon S3 without SSL.

translation: The server could not connect to its file storage: {{.error}}. File uploads and downloads may fail.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the file storage connection test failed; {{.error}} is the error returned by the test, in English.

translation: The connection test to file storage failed on {{.nodes}}, while the other nodes reach it, so file uploads and downloads through those nodes may fail. Check the network, firewall, proxy and DNS settings on those nodes. For local storage, also check that the shared directory is mounted on them. Error: {{.error}}
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the file storage connection test fails on some cluster nodes but not others; {{.nodes}} is a comma-separated list of node hostnames and {{.error}} is the error the failing nodes reported.

translation: Check the file storage settings, then use Test Connection in System Console > Environment > File Storage. For local storage, check that FileSettings.Directory exists and the Mattermost user can write to it. For Amazon S3, check the bucket, endpoint and credentials.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a failed file storage connection test; 'Test Connection' and 'System Console > Environment > File Storage' name System Console elements; 'FileSettings.Directory' is a config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: File storage connection test failed
description: Health dashboard finding title when the server could not connect to its file storage (local directory or cloud bucket).

translation: The latest finished {{.job_type}} run ({{.job_id}}) ended in error: {{.error}}
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a background job's most recent finished run failed; {{.job_type}} is the job type identifier (such as ldap_sync) and {{.job_id}} is the job's ID, neither should be translated; {{.error}} is the error message the job recorded.

translation: The latest finished {{.job_type}} run ({{.job_id}}) ended in error without recording an error message.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a background job's most recent finished run failed and no error message was recorded; {{.job_type}} is the job type identifier (such as ldap_sync) and {{.job_id}} is the job's ID, neither should be translated.

translation: Review the job's error and the server logs at the failed run's start time to find the cause. Common causes to rule out: database load, connection pool limits, network or failover events, and statement timeouts. Resolve it, then run the job again and confirm it completes. Until a run succeeds, the job's work (directory sync, compliance export, data retention or search indexing) is not being done.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a background job whose latest run failed.

translation: Latest job run failed
description: Health dashboard finding title when the most recent finished run of a background job (such as AD/LDAP sync or data retention) ended in error.

translation: The {{.job_type}} job {{.job_id}} is in progress but has recorded no activity for {{.hours}} hours. This usually means the worker died mid-run or the scheduler is wedged.
description: Health dashboard finding detail for a background job that is still marked in progress but has stopped reporting activity; {{.job_type}} is the job type identifier (such as ldap_sync) and {{.job_id}} is the job's ID, neither should be translated; {{.hours}} is a whole number of hours.

translation: Cancel the stuck job from its System Console page, with mmctl job cancel, or through the API. Check the server logs around the job's last activity, then run it again.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a background job stuck in progress; 'mmctl job cancel' is a command and should not be translated.

translation: Job stuck in progress for more than 24 hours
description: Health dashboard finding title when a background job has been marked in progress with no activity for over 24 hours.

translation: The {{.job_type}} job {{.job_id}} has reported no progress and has recorded no activity for more than an hour. This usually means the worker died, deadlocked, or lost its database connection before the first batch.
description: Health dashboard finding detail for a background job that is in progress but has neither reported progress nor recorded activity for over an hour; {{.job_type}} is the job type identifier (such as ldap_sync) and {{.job_id}} is the job's ID, neither should be translated.

translation: Cancel the job from its System Console page, with mmctl job cancel, or through the API. Check the server logs from the job's start time for panics or connection errors, then run it again. If it recurs, capture a goroutine profile from /debug/pprof/goroutine on the metrics server while the job is stuck.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a background job running with no progress; 'mmctl job cancel' is a command and '/debug/pprof/goroutine' is a URL path, neither should be translated. 'Goroutine profile' is a Go debugging snapshot of running threads.

translation: Job in progress with no progress or activity for more than an hour
description: Health dashboard finding title when a background job is in progress but has neither reported progress nor recorded activity for over an hour.

translation: IdAttribute is {{.attribute}}. Mattermost links each account to its directory entry by this attribute, so when a user's email changes (marriage, rebrand, department move) the link breaks and the user can no longer reach their existing account.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the AD/LDAP ID attribute is an email attribute. {{.attribute}} is the configured attribute name. 'IdAttribute', 'objectGUID', 'entryUUID' and the command 'mmctl ldap idmigrate' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: Switch IdAttribute to a stable attribute such as objectGUID (AD) or entryUUID (OpenLDAP), then migrate existing accounts with mmctl ldap idmigrate.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the AD/LDAP ID attribute is an email attribute. 'IdAttribute', 'objectGUID', 'entryUUID' and the command 'mmctl ldap idmigrate' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: LDAP IdAttribute is an email attribute
description: Health dashboard finding title when the AD/LDAP ID attribute is an email attribute. 'IdAttribute', 'objectGUID', 'entryUUID' and the command 'mmctl ldap idmigrate' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: Port 636 conventionally expects implicit TLS (LDAPS), but ConnectionSecurity is None or STARTTLS. This combination is usually a misconfiguration, but it can be valid behind a TLS-terminating proxy. Verify that LDAP sign-in and sync are succeeding.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the AD/LDAP port is 636 but the connection security is None or STARTTLS. 'ConnectionSecurity', 'None', 'TLS', 'STARTTLS' and 'LDAPS' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: If LDAP sign-in or sync is failing, set ConnectionSecurity to TLS for port 636. If they are working, no change is needed.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the AD/LDAP port is 636 but the connection security is None or STARTTLS. 'ConnectionSecurity', 'None', 'TLS', 'STARTTLS' and 'LDAPS' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: LDAP port 636 configured without ConnectionSecurity=TLS
description: Health dashboard finding title when the AD/LDAP port is 636 but the connection security is None or STARTTLS. 'ConnectionSecurity', 'None', 'TLS', 'STARTTLS' and 'LDAPS' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: Port 389 is conventionally plaintext or STARTTLS, while implicit TLS (LDAPS) conventionally uses 636. This combination is usually a misconfiguration, but it can be valid behind a TLS-terminating proxy or a deliberately reconfigured server. Verify that LDAP sign-in and sync are succeeding.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the AD/LDAP port is 389 but the connection security is TLS. 'ConnectionSecurity', 'TLS', 'STARTTLS' and 'LDAPS' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: If LDAP sign-in or sync is failing, use port 636 for TLS or switch ConnectionSecurity to STARTTLS for port 389. If they are working, no change is needed.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the AD/LDAP port is 389 but the connection security is TLS. 'ConnectionSecurity', 'TLS', 'STARTTLS' and 'LDAPS' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: LDAP port 389 configured with ConnectionSecurity=TLS
description: Health dashboard finding title when the AD/LDAP port is 389 but the connection security is TLS. 'ConnectionSecurity', 'TLS', 'STARTTLS' and 'LDAPS' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: The LDAP test (connect, bind and a user search) failed, so LDAP sign-in and sync may be failing.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the AD/LDAP connection test run by the server failed. 'LdapServer', 'LdapPort', 'ConnectionSecurity' and the button label 'Test Connection' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: The LDAP test (connect, bind and a user search) failed on {{.nodes}}, while the other nodes reach the LDAP server, so LDAP sign-in may fail on those nodes. Check the network, firewall, proxy and DNS settings on those nodes.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the LDAP connection test fails on some cluster nodes but not others; {{.nodes}} is a comma-separated list of node hostnames.

translation: Check the error details, then confirm LdapServer, LdapPort, ConnectionSecurity and the bind credentials, and that the Mattermost servers can reach the LDAP server. Use Test Connection on the AD/LDAP page to check again.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the AD/LDAP connection test run by the server failed. 'LdapServer', 'LdapPort', 'ConnectionSecurity' and the button label 'Test Connection' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: LDAP connection test failed
description: Health dashboard finding title when the AD/LDAP connection test run by the server failed. 'LdapServer', 'LdapPort', 'ConnectionSecurity' and the button label 'Test Connection' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: QueryTimeout is {{.timeout}} seconds. Tight timeouts cause spurious LDAP sign-in and sync failures on slow directories.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the AD/LDAP query timeout is shorter than 10 seconds. {{.timeout}} is the configured timeout in seconds. 'QueryTimeout' and 'LdapSettings.QueryTimeout' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: Raise LdapSettings.QueryTimeout to 60 seconds (the default).
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when the AD/LDAP query timeout is shorter than 10 seconds. 'QueryTimeout' and 'LdapSettings.QueryTimeout' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: LDAP QueryTimeout is below 10 seconds
description: Health dashboard finding title when the AD/LDAP query timeout is shorter than 10 seconds. 'QueryTimeout' and 'LdapSettings.QueryTimeout' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: {{.users}} active user accounts are managed manually. Mattermost recommends single sign-on once a workspace has more than 100 users: manual account management at this scale leads to stale accounts, onboarding lag, and offboarding drift, each of which is a security and licensing risk.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a workspace with more than 100 users uses no single sign-on provider (AD/LDAP, SAML, GitLab, Google, Office 365 or OpenID Connect). {{.users}} is the number of active user accounts. 'AD/LDAP', 'SAML' and 'OpenID Connect' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: Connect Mattermost to your identity provider: AD/LDAP if you run a directory, otherwise SAML or OpenID Connect.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when a workspace with more than 100 users uses no single sign-on provider (AD/LDAP, SAML, GitLab, Google, Office 365 or OpenID Connect). 'AD/LDAP', 'SAML' and 'OpenID Connect' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: Over 100 users with no single sign-on
description: Health dashboard finding title when a workspace with more than 100 users uses no single sign-on provider (AD/LDAP, SAML, GitLab, Google, Office 365 or OpenID Connect). 'AD/LDAP', 'SAML' and 'OpenID Connect' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: Mattermost does not verify the LDAP server's TLS certificate, so connections to the directory are open to man-in-the-middle attacks. This is acceptable only for development and testing.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when AD/LDAP certificate verification is turned off. 'SkipCertificateVerification' is a config name and should not be translated.

translation: Install the LDAP server's CA chain on the Mattermost servers and set SkipCertificateVerification to false.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when AD/LDAP certificate verification is turned off. 'SkipCertificateVerification' is a config name and should not be translated.

translation: LDAP SkipCertificateVerification is enabled
description: Health dashboard finding title when AD/LDAP certificate verification is turned off. 'SkipCertificateVerification' is a config name and should not be translated.

translation: SyncIntervalMinutes is {{.interval_minutes}}, and recent LDAP sync runs averaged {{.avg_run_seconds}} seconds, {{.duty_pct}}% of the interval. Long runs on a short interval keep database load elevated and can add replica lag.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when each AD/LDAP sync run takes at least a quarter of the sync interval. {{.interval_minutes}} is the sync interval in minutes, {{.avg_run_seconds}} the average run length in seconds and {{.duty_pct}} the percentage of the interval. 'SyncIntervalMinutes', 'LdapSettings.UserFilter' and 'BaseDN' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: No LDAP sync run with a measurable duration was found.
description: Health dashboard reason shown when the AD/LDAP sync duration check found no finished sync runs to measure, so its status is unknown.

translation: Narrow LdapSettings.UserFilter and BaseDN to scope the directory walk, or lengthen SyncIntervalMinutes. Aim for sync runs that take less than 25% of the interval.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when each AD/LDAP sync run takes at least a quarter of the sync interval. 'SyncIntervalMinutes', 'LdapSettings.UserFilter' and 'BaseDN' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: LDAP sync runs for a large share of its interval
description: Health dashboard finding title when each AD/LDAP sync run takes at least a quarter of the sync interval. 'SyncIntervalMinutes', 'LdapSettings.UserFilter' and 'BaseDN' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: LDAP sync searches the directory from BaseDN, so with it empty the sync cannot find the users it should update.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when AD/LDAP sync is enabled but no base DN is set. 'BaseDN' and 'LdapSettings.BaseDN' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: Set LdapSettings.BaseDN to the directory root you want to sync.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when AD/LDAP sync is enabled but no base DN is set. 'BaseDN' and 'LdapSettings.BaseDN' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: LDAP sync enabled but BaseDN is empty
description: Health dashboard finding title when AD/LDAP sync is enabled but no base DN is set. 'BaseDN' and 'LdapSettings.BaseDN' are config or product names and should not be translated.

translation: The license expired on {{.expires_at}}. The server removes an expired license 10 days after it expires, and Enterprise features stop working.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the license has expired; {{.expires_at}} is the expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD).

translation: The trial license expired on {{.expires_at}}. The server removes an expired license 10 days after it expires, and Enterprise features stop working.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a trial license has expired; {{.expires_at}} is the expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD).

translation: Get a new license and upload it in System Console > About > Edition and License.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for an expired license; 'System Console > About > Edition and License' is the path to the license page in the admin UI.

translation: License has expired
description: Health dashboard finding title when the server's license expired before the health data was collected.

translation: The license expires on {{.expires_at}}.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the license expires within 30 days; {{.expires_at}} is the expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD).

translation: The trial license expires on {{.expires_at}}.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a trial license expires within 30 days; {{.expires_at}} is the expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD).

translation: Get a new license now, so it can be uploaded in System Console > About > Edition and License before the current one expires.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a license that expires soon; 'System Console > About > Edition and License' is the path to the license page in the admin UI.

translation: License expires within 30 days
description: Health dashboard finding title when the server's license expires in less than 30 days.

translation: LogSettings.FileLevel is {{.level}}. Debug-level file logging grows log files quickly, and the extra detail can include request payloads. This is fine while troubleshooting, but not ideal as a steady-state production setting.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the file log level is debug or trace; {{.level}} is the configured level. 'LogSettings.FileLevel' is a config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: If you are not actively troubleshooting, set LogSettings.FileLevel to INFO to reduce log volume.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a debug or trace file log level; 'LogSettings.FileLevel' is a config setting path and 'INFO' is a setting value; do not translate them.

translation: File logging at debug or trace level
description: Health dashboard finding title when the server writes its log file at the very verbose debug or trace level.

translation: LogSettings.EnableFile is false, so the server writes no log file. Support Packets then contain no server logs, even if an external collector captures stdout or journald, and troubleshooting with Mattermost Support takes longer.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when file logging is turned off; 'LogSettings.EnableFile' is a config setting path, 'stdout' and 'journald' are log destinations, and a 'sidecar' is a helper container; do not translate them.

translation: Set LogSettings.EnableFile to true. This works alongside console logging, so an existing log collector keeps working.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for disabled file logging; 'LogSettings.EnableFile' is a config setting path and should not be translated.

translation: File logging disabled
description: Health dashboard finding title when the server does not write a log file.

translation: TeamSettings.MaxNotificationsPerChannel is {{.limit}}, so @channel, @all and @here still work in channels with thousands of members. A single channel-wide mention there fans out thousands of notifications at once, which causes latency spikes.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when the per-channel notification limit is above 5000; {{.limit}} is the configured limit, 'TeamSettings.MaxNotificationsPerChannel' is the config setting path and '@channel', '@all' and '@here' are Mattermost mentions, none should be translated.

translation: Lower TeamSettings.MaxNotificationsPerChannel to 5000 or less (the default is 1000). @channel, @all and @here are disabled once a channel reaches this many members, so check with the teams that use them in large channels first.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a high per-channel notification limit; 'TeamSettings.MaxNotificationsPerChannel' is the config setting path and '@channel', '@all' and '@here' are Mattermost mentions, none should be translated.

translation: Channel-wide mentions allowed in very large channels
description: Health dashboard finding title when the per-channel notification limit is above 5000, so @channel, @all and @here work in channels with thousands of members; '@channel', '@all' and '@here' are Mattermost mentions and should not be translated.

translation: MetricsSettings.Enable is false. Metrics are optional, and many deployments do not run Prometheus. If you want runtime visibility into database connections, HTTP latency and goroutine counts, enabling metrics provides it.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when Prometheus metrics are turned off, which is a valid choice; 'MetricsSettings.Enable' is a config setting path and 'Prometheus' is a product name; do not translate them.

translation: If you use Prometheus, set MetricsSettings.Enable to true and scrape the metrics listener (port 8067 by default).
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for disabled Prometheus metrics; 'MetricsSettings.Enable' is a config setting path and 'scrape' is the Prometheus term for collecting metrics.

translation: Prometheus metrics disabled (optional)
description: Health dashboard finding title when Prometheus performance metrics are turned off; the finding is informational because metrics are optional.

translation: The container's memory working set is {{.working_set}} MB of its {{.limit}} MB limit. If it keeps growing, the kernel may kill the server or a plugin process.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a node's container uses at least 90% of its memory limit; {{.working_set}} is the non-reclaimable memory in MB and {{.limit}} is the container limit in MB.

translation: Reduce memory use by Mattermost and its plugins, or raise the container memory limit. Keep enough headroom for plugin processes, the Go runtime and traffic spikes.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when a node's container is close to its memory limit; 'Go' is the programming language name.

translation: Container memory nearly exhausted
description: Health dashboard finding title when a server node's container memory working set is at least 90% of its limit.

translation: The container has recorded {{.kills}} out-of-memory kills since it started. The killed process may have been a plugin or another child process; review the plugin list and the container memory limit.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a node's cgroup recorded an OOM kill; {{.kills}} is the number of processes killed, and 'plugin' means a Mattermost server plugin.

translation: Review the plugin processes and container logs to identify what was killed, then reduce its memory use or raise the container memory limit.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when a process in a Mattermost server container was killed for running out of memory.

translation: A container process was killed for running out of memory
description: Health dashboard finding title when a server node's cgroup reports one or more OOM kills.

translation: The container was throttled during {{.throttled}} of {{.periods}} CPU scheduling periods. Sustained CPU throttling can make Mattermost slow even when host CPU usage looks low.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a node's container has been CPU-throttled in at least 10% of its scheduling periods; {{.throttled}} is the number of throttled periods and {{.periods}} is the total number of periods.

translation: Raise the container CPU limit, or remove the limit while keeping a CPU request.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for sustained container CPU throttling. 'CPU limit' and 'CPU request' are Kubernetes resource terms.

translation: Container CPU throttling is high
description: Health dashboard finding title when a server node's container is throttled during at least 10% of CPU scheduling periods.

translation: The server process has {{.open}} of {{.max}} file descriptors open. Once it reaches the limit, new connections and file operations fail.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when a node is close to its open file limit; {{.open}} is the number of open file descriptors and {{.max}} is the limit.

translation: Raise the open file limit: set LimitNOFILE in the Mattermost systemd unit, or raise the nofile ulimit of the container, then restart the server.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step for a node close to its open file limit; 'LimitNOFILE' is a systemd setting and 'nofile' is a ulimit name; do not translate them.

translation: File descriptors nearly exhausted
description: Health dashboard finding title when a server node uses 90% or more of its open file descriptor limit.

translation: The Go memory limit is {{.go_limit}} MB, but the container limit is {{.container_limit}} MB. The garbage collector may not work harder before the kernel kills the process.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when GOMEMLIMIT is at least the container memory limit; {{.go_limit}} and {{.container_limit}} are values in MB, and 'Go' is the programming language name.

translation: Set GOMEMLIMIT to about 80–90% of the container memory limit, leaving headroom for memory outside the Go heap and for plugin processes.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when GOMEMLIMIT is too high for the container; 'GOMEMLIMIT' is a Go runtime environment variable and should not be translated.

translation: Go memory limit is at or above the container limit
description: Health dashboard finding title when GOMEMLIMIT is equal to or greater than the container memory limit; 'Go' is the programming language name.

translation: GOMAXPROCS is {{.go_max_procs}}, above the container CPU limit of {{.cpu_limit}} CPUs. The extra runnable threads can increase CPU throttling.
description: Health dashboard finding detail when Go can run more threads simultaneously than a node's container CPU quota; {{.go_max_procs}} is GOMAXPROCS and {{.cpu_limit}} is the CPU limit in CPUs. 'GOMAXPROCS' is a Go runtime setting and should not be translated.

translation: Unset GOMAXPROCS so the Go runtime sizes it to the container CPU limit, then restart the server.
description: Health dashboard fix-it step when GOMAXPROCS exceeds a node's container CPU quota. 'GOMAXPROCS' is a Go runtime setting and should not be translated.

translation: GOMAXPROCS exceeds the container CPU limit
description: Health dashboard finding title when Go can run more threads simultaneously than a server node's container CPU quota. 'GOMAXPROCS' is a Go runtime setting and should not be translated.

translation: The 15-minute host load average is {{.load}} across {{.cores}} CPU cores. A sustained load of two or more tasks per core can indicate CPU or I/O pressure.
